If your home was built between 1950 and 1990, there's a chance your electrical panel is literally uninsurable. Here's what to look for.

Federal Pacific Electric (FPE) Stab-Lok panels and Zinsco panels were installed in millions of American homes during that era. The problem? They're known to fail silently — breakers that don't trip when they should, which means no protection when a circuit overloads. Some insurance companies in Texas will flat-out deny coverage or refuse to renew a policy if they find one of these panels during a home inspection. We've replaced them in homes across DFW — Rowlett, Garland, McKinney, Dallas, Plano. The job takes one day. The peace of mind lasts a lot longer. Not sure what brand your panel is? Pull up your phone, go to your breaker box, and look for the name on the door. If it says "Federal Pacific," "Stab-Lok," or "Zinsco" — give us a call. Free phone estimate. We'll tell you exactly what you're dealing with and what it costs to fix it. No pressure, no upsell, just a straight answer from a local electrician who actually cares about your family's safety.

#DFW #FederalPacificPanel #PanelReplacement #DallasElectrician #GrizzlyElectrical #HomeElectrical #RowlettTX

Call (469) 863-9804 right now — free phone estimate, 5 minutes, straight answers.

You spent $50,000 on an EV. You're still charging it with a regular wall outlet?

A standard 120V outlet charges your EV about 4 miles of range per hour. A Level 2 charger? Up to 30 miles per hour. That's the difference between waking up to a full charge every morning and waking up to 40% and a problem. We install Level 2 home chargers across DFW — Tesla Wall Connectors, J1772, universal. We handle the permit, the wiring, and the inspection. No surprises on the bill.

If your electrical panel says "Federal Pacific" or "Zinsco" on it — your homeowner's insurance company may already know something you don't.

These panel brands have a reputation. Some insurance companies won't cover homes that still have them. Others will drop your policy at renewal. And beyond the insurance issue, there are real safety concerns — Federal Pacific Stab-Lok breakers have a documented history of failing to trip during overloads. If you don't know what brand your panel is, go look right now. If it says either of those names, give us a call. We'll come take a look and tell you exactly where you stand.
